question: None shared. P-117 (Aljalal et al. 2024; the right PDF is 1-s2.0-S1746809423008959, and the pack file pdf/P-117.txt is an MRI-PET fusion paper) classifies MCI vs HC (binary) from resting-state EEG. P-5 (Gao et al. 2023) classifies MCI vs AD vs CN (three-class) from fundus photographs plus OCT. The channels (EEG against eye/retina), the comparison and the cohorts all differ.
metric: Mismatch: P-117's figure is accuracy, while P-5's 84.96% is the per-class precision for MCI inside a three-class model.

figures.P-117: Binary MCI vs HC accuracy 99.81% (11 NSGA-selected channels, ensemble KNN) and 99.51% with all channels, 10-fold CV over 3660 EEG segments from 61 participants (29 amnestic MCI/32 HC). Wilson with subject n=61: 0.9981 -> (0.937, 1.000).
figures.P-5: MCI-class precision 84.96% within a three-class model; three-class accuracy 91.64%, AUC 96.78%, 5-fold CV, first dataset 117 patients (29 MCI/58 eyes, 50 CN/100 eyes, 38 AD/76 eyes).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure: P-5 prints no binary MCI-vs-CN accuracy and P-117 no three-class or retinal result.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% (and 99.51% full-channel) from internal 10-fold CV over segments of only 61 participants, with no external cohort. The registry's performance_suspect=false arises only because its Best_Metric reads 'not reported'. P-5's 96.78% AUC is below 0.97.
reason: The pair fails condition 1 (EEG against retinal imaging; binary against three-class) and condition 2 (accuracy against class-specific precision), and P-117 meets the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5). The claimed disagreement exists only because the record labels P-5's MCI-class precision as a T1 accuracy-like result (condition 6). No uncertainty comparison is meaningful across different metric types, so beyond_uncertainty is recorded as false, meaning not assessable.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method. (document: 1-s2.0-S1746809423008959)
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training
divided into 3660 segments (1740 segments from MCI cases and 1860 from HC cases)
The proposed method achieved high precision rates of 84.96% and 80.90% in classifying MCI and positive test scores for cognitive impairment, respectively.
As shown in Table 2, the proposed network DuCAN had an accuracy of 91.64% and an AUC of 96.78%.
